title: Russian famine of 1891–1892
text: The 1891–1892 famine in the Russian Empire, sometimes called the Tsar Famine, Tsar's Famine or Black Earth Famine, began along the Volga River and spread as far as the Urals and the Black Sea. This area included the provinces of Nizhni-Novgorod, Ryazan, Tula, Kazan, Simbirsk, Saratov, Penza, Samara and Tambov. The famine was initially caused by poor weather and was exacerbated by poor logistical networks, and a lack of grain reserves due to the Russian government's export policy.
